rows.note: This is the all-purpose way to say that something moves or points eastward.
This is the all-purpose noun for the compass direction east.

example.english: The sun rises in the east.
example.jyutping: taai3 joeng4 hai2 dung1 bin1 sing1 hei2

rows.note: Use this for the east side or eastern area of a place rather than a compass label alone.

example.english: There’s a park on the east side of our building.
example.traditional: 我哋間屋東面有個公園。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gaan1 uk1 dung1 min6 jau5 go3 gung1 jyun4

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose adjective for something situated on the east side.

example.english: The house on the east side is by the sea.
example.jyutping: dung1 bin1 ge3 uk1 kei2 hai2 hoi2 bin1

rows.note: Use this when the thing is oriented or moving eastward rather than merely located on the east side.

example.english: The train heading east is about to leave.
example.jyutping: hoeng3 dung1 ge3 lit6 ce1 zau6 faai3 hoi1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for an eastern region or eastern section, especially in geographical descriptions.

example.english: There are many factories in the east of this city.
example.traditional: 呢個城市東部有好多工廠。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 sing4 si5 dung1 bou6 jau5 hou2 do1 gung1 cong2

rows.note: Use this when the sense is the people living in the eastern area.

example.english: People from the east like spicy food.
example.jyutping: dung1 min6 ge3 jan4 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6

rows.jyutping: jau4 dung1 min6 ceoi1 lai4 ge3 N
rows.note: Use this before 風 or another noun when it is blowing or coming from the east.

example.english: The wind blowing from the east is quite strong today.
example.traditional: 由東面吹嚟嘅風今日幾大。
example.jyutping: jau4 dung1 min6 ceoi1 lai4 ge3 fung1 gam1 jat6 gei2 daai6
